checks: The positive power with exponent beta/(r+1)>=1 is convex and nondecreasing on the positive range of f^(-1/beta), so its composition is finite, positive and convex on the same full-dimensional open support. Finiteness and convexity also give continuity on U.

For any positive-mass closed convex L, the positive set U intersect int L is open, nonempty and has full restricted measure because the boundary of full-dimensional L is null. In the verified hereditary-depth argument of 23a563a735c07c25, compact convex inner exhaustions give bounded upper semicontinuous truncations with convex extended inverse power. The bound passes to the supremum for the untruncated restriction by monotone mass convergence and halfspace monotonicity.

Attainment is needed in the open positive set. Through-point halfspace masses are jointly continuous by hyperplane nullity and dominated convergence. The minimum over the compact unit sphere is continuous. An outward halfspace bounds depth by the vanishing total-mass tail, while any point outside the open convex positive set has a containing halfspace of zero mass by separation. Positive maximal depth is therefore attained in U intersect int L, regardless of boundedness.

For A_i>alpha, tail mass starts at A_i at b_i (hyperplanes are null), is continuous and tends to zero. Since 0<A_i-alpha<A_i, some finite threshold lies strictly past b_i. Union bounding removed tails gives retained mass at least M-R, and each cap retains at most alpha, whether cut or not. If M-R<=0, adding alpha/gamma_r>0 already gives strictness.

For M-R>0, the open cover puts the hereditary point y strictly inside some H_i. A sufficiently small ball around y is contained in U intersect int L intersect int H_i, and f is bounded below there by continuity and positivity at y. The ball half strictly outside the through-y subcap therefore gives positive loss, and the through-y subcap has restricted mass at least gamma_r times the retained mass. No coverage of boundary points of U is needed.

dependencies.mapping: The hereditary-depth lemma in its proof applies to the present f in dimension r after convex power composition, and to each positive-mass closed convex L formed by trimming. It gives a point in U intersect int L of depth at least gamma_r times restricted mass.

Its tail-cut construction uses finite hyperplane-null measure and proper halfspaces, both satisfied. The proof reproduces that construction in the whole space and invokes the strict open cover only at the interior hereditary point, so the predecessor theorem’s closed-support cover hypothesis is not imposed here.

overlap.comparison: Supplies the same weak positive-part profile from hereditary depth for closed support covers. Open interiors and attainment at a locally positive density point yield the genuinely stronger strict inequality here.
Supplies the attained hereditary density-depth ingredient and a non-strict effective cap-count theorem for ordinary convex bodies. Its weak conclusion does not supply the open-cover strictness.

Its equality classification implies open-cover strictness for uniform convex bodies with exactly D+1 caps in D>=2, since canonical simplex vertex-cap interiors miss their centroid. The present density result permits arbitrary finite cap count, unbounded support and nonuniform inverse-power convex densities.
